shouldFix.title: Adoption makes DR-133's cell clause 'no contract exists' false, and the entry neither says so nor names the repair — while citing as its form three precedents that did land the recording in the cell
shouldFix.finding: DR-133's live status cell at file 08 7585325d reads: '**OPEN** — no contract exists. Not eligible in kind today (D-133). Not SATISFIED.' The moment this entry is adopted, a dual-ACCEPT design contract exists, and that clause is false. The subject never mentions it: measured, 'no contract exists' occurs zero times in the draft and 'MF-6' occurs zero times, so neither the staleness nor an owed repair is recorded. The form citation makes the gap visible rather than excusing it. The draft says 'Same form as D-013 / D-015 / D-035 / D-116', but three of those four reflected the recording in the row cell — DR-103 carries 'OPEN — design contract ACCEPTED 2026-08-13 (D-013)', DR-114 carries '(D-035)', DR-102 carries 'Design contract ACCEPTED 2026-08-13 (D-015)' — and none of those three entries contains a does-not-edit-file-08 clause. Only D-116 followed the branch this entry follows, and that was safe there precisely because DR-117's cell is a bare 'OPEN' asserting nothing. DR-133's cell asserts something, so the D-116 precedent does not carry. The corpus has just settled how to handle this: D-133 recorded its COORD annotation as 'Owed later work, not performed here', and D-135's own cycle established that an act which falsifies live text must name the repair even when it cannot perform it.

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 2 SHOULD-FIX. Fifteen attacks run, three landed. Custody is intact: subject b4b4b475 at 0444 unmoved, HEAD never left 52ea851, file 08 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree, and all six measured-inputs rows reproduce including both v3 verdict files. The central claim holds: v3 is a genuine dual ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX from both reviewers, measured from the cited files. I also tested the inference most likely to be drawn from that — that a dual ACCEPT at 0 blockers opens D-056 Class A — and it fails, so Decision 2's refusal is substantively right rather than merely cautious: D-133's Class A requires application-grade acceptance with no express reservation, while v3 is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING, and both acceptances are expressly candidate-grade. I confirmed D-135 executed as reviewed: file 08 now carries 4 of 32 twice, no 4 of 30, 65 rows, and the 2026-08-15 snapshot heading. What blocks is recording completeness. First, adopting this entry makes DR-133's live cell clause 'no contract exists' false, and the draft neither acknowledges it nor names a repair — zero occurrences of that clause or of MF-6. The form citation sharpens rather than excuses it: three of the four precedents the entry names as its form landed the recording in the row cell, and none of those three carries a does-not-edit-file-08 clause; only D-116 followed this branch, and that was safe because DR-117's cell asserts nothing. DR-133's cell asserts something. D-133's own 'owed later work, not performed here' pattern is the available fix. Second, Decision 3 routes 'Claude advisories' when three advisories exist across the two pinned verdicts — mine plus Codex's POOCV3-ADV1, which independently reaches the same substance as my ADV-2 — and names none by identifier, where D-131's precedent names them. Both repairs are additive; everything the entry decides is correct and should carry into turn 2 unchanged.
